key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of unseen perovskite samples, helping predict stability faster than conventional aging tests.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable way to screen perovskite formulations and prioritize promising photovoltaic materials with less experimental time and cost.
method: Collected >86k PL spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress
Featurized time-series spectra with a physics-informed representation
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity and generalize to unseen samples
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on a diverse dataset spanning different crystallinities and compositions and was reported to outperform baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Forecast accuracy may depend on the quality and coverage of the training stress conditions, so extrapolation to very different degradation regimes should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
